global_issues.title: US-Iran conflict escalates with Hormuz tanker attacks, oil surges
global_issues.note: Confirmed ongoing: UAE tankers hit by Iranian missiles in Omani waters, US conducting repeated strikes on Iranian targets (including a dozen targets overnight July 29-30). WTI trading $83-85 range, off a 6.6% single-day surge, now consolidating/slightly down (-0.7%) on July 30 as some reports of improving Hormuz transit flow emerge. Briefing's 'closed recently amid partial de-escalation' framing is roughly right but risk remains acute, not de-escalating cleanly — a 10-day ceasefire proposal has been floated but not confirmed adopted.

global_issues.title: Trump 25% tariff on NVDA chips to China remains in force
global_issues.note: Confirmed: 25% tariff on Nvidia H200 (and AMD MI325X) chips exported to China signed January 14, 2026, remains active. Case-by-case licensing continues; Chinese customs has reportedly been blocking some shipments and Beijing has pushed back on the tariff collection mechanism, an added friction point not mentioned in the briefing.

global_issues.title: Russia-Ukraine war continues with fresh strikes on Kyiv infrastructure
global_issues.note: Understated. This was not just 'fresh strikes within 8-27 days' — a major overnight barrage (70+ missiles, 280+ drones) hit Ukraine within the last 24h (night of July 29-30), killing at least 8-10 civilians including children, with a Russian missile/cruise missile entering Polish airspace and NATO scrambling fighter jets. This is a materially larger escalation (NATO airspace incident) than the briefing's generic description conveys.

grok_report.summary: The geopolitical narrative (Iran/Hormuz, NVDA tariffs, Russia-Ukraine) is largely accurate but somewhat understates the severity of the overnight Ukraine escalation (NATO airspace incident). The critical flaw is on the market side: the briefing appears to be missing Microsoft's blowout Q4 earnings and the resulting ~14-15% stock surge that drove a broad tech rally, causing its MSFT price data, overall market mood ('yellow, mixed'), and sector narrative (tech 'pressured') to conflict with the actual, more bullish close on July 30. AAPL and AMZN price moves do check out against their real earnings-driven catalysts, though the briefing omits the earnings context for both.
